lines.text: Two crowns. Two curses. One was ranked the best team on Earth and never won a thing. The other ruled a whole continent seven times... and never won a single World Cup match. Tonight, one of them breaks.
And an old scribe is keeping score.
Last time, we imagined Spain and Cape Verde — and that was OUR prediction, our story, not a result. Tonight, two kings who were never crowned collide for real.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends, episode eighteen. Belgium versus Egypt. The Red Devils... and the Pharaohs.
And stay with me — because in the final minutes, a golden generation faces the one ghost it has never beaten: itself.
First, the history. In nineteen thirty-four, Egypt became the first African and Arab nation ever to play at a World Cup.
And here is the part nobody tells you. Egypt have won Africa a record seven times — yet across three World Cups, they have never won a single match. Seven crowns... and one unbroken curse.
Belgium carry a curse of their own. For nearly four years they were ranked the number one team on the planet — and walked away with nothing.
A golden generation. The semi-final of twenty eighteen. The talent of a lifetime. And not one trophy to show the world.
Tonight is, almost certainly, their last dance together.
So meet the Red Devils. At the heart, Kevin De Bruyne — the conductor, the passer who sees the game three seconds before anyone else.
Up front, Romelu Lukaku — Belgium's greatest goalscorer, all power and hunger.
And on the wing, the future: Jeremy Doku, electric, fearless, the bridge to whatever comes next.
Behind them, Courtois — a wall in gloves. This is a team built to finally finish the story.
But across the line wait the Pharaohs — and they have a king of their own.
Mohamed Salah. The captain. The talisman who carries a nation on his shoulders, chasing the World Cup stage that has eluded him for years.
Beside him, Omar Marmoush — pace and fire from the Premier League — and a disciplined Egyptian spine that does not break easily.
When the uncrowned number one meets the seven-time kings... someone's curse has to die.
And the duel inside the match: De Bruyne against Salah. The conductor against the king. Vision against will.
Our prediction — built on Belgian experience, on one last dance, and on one flash of Salah magic that refuses to be silenced. Watch.
Belgium strike first. De Bruyne threads the impossible pass, Lukaku finishes like he was born to. The golden generation lead. One-nil.
But you do not write off a king. Salah cuts inside, drops the shoulder, and curls one home. One-all. A whole continent rises.
The ghost is awake now. Could this be the night Egypt finally win? The clock turns red. The Pharaohs believe.
And then — Doku. The young one, the future, drives at the heart of it and squares for the winner. Two-one Belgium.
Two-one at the whistle, in our story. The golden generation cling to their last dance. And Egypt's century-old curse survives one more night.
But Salah scored. The king reminded the world he belongs on the biggest stage — and that the next chapter is still unwritten.
Do you agree? Comment DEVILS if Belgium's golden generation finally delivers. Comment PHARAOHS if Salah breaks the curse and shocks them.
And the old scribe between the benches? Legend number eighteen: the Keeper of the Two Crowns. For a hundred years he has recorded every great team football forgot to reward.
Tonight he held two empty cases — ranked first, and seven times kings — waiting to see whose curse would crack. Collect him inside the game.
Which brings us to YOU. At WorldCup twenty-six dot world, pick three of the forty-eight nations — and every goal they score... scores for you.
Free to play. Climb the leaderboard, just for fun. No prizes.
Hit like — send this to the friend who still believes Salah can break the curse. And subscribe: the legends are only beginning.
